To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the reconfigurable mesh can be used for efficient computation of the Hough transform, and that (ii) buses can be used as computational devices in addition to communication devices.

(1) the Hough transform can be efficiently computed on a reconfigurable architecture, and (2) the Hough algorithm is the first example of a parallel computational algorithm for which buses play a crucial role in the computation of the algorithm.
buses are not only useful as topological descriptors, but also as computational devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of efficient algorithms for the Hough transform, using a reconfigurable bus architecture.
the development of new computational models, algorithms, and architectures for the efficient solution of image processing and computer vision problems.
the design of efficient and scalable algorithms on reconfigurable mesh computers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hough transform can be computed on a reconfigurable machine in a time which is linear with respect to the image size and logarithmic with respect to the number of angles.
buses are not just a means to an end but can also be a powerful computational device.
the Hough transform can be successfully implemented in reconfigurable meshes with the help of buses, and that the resulting algorithms are very efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to present a parallel algorithm for the Hough transform that uses buses as topological descriptors as well as computational devices.
the Hough transform can be computed in O ( n × N ) time on a reconfigurable architecture with a bus size of O (log( N / n )).
the Hough transform can be computed on a reconfigurable bus mesh in O (log( N / n ) × ( n + log N )) time and O ( N ) processors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Hough transform, which is traditionally computed on a serial processor, can be computed on a parallel reconfigurable machine with the same asymptotic complexity as the best known sequential algorithms.
reconfigurable meshes are a viable architecture for image processing and computer vision applications.
, by judiciously using buses as both computational devices and as topological descriptors, it is possible to achieve a speed-up of the order of log( N /n) over the best known sequential algorithms.
